newsitem.title: CHINA: BASF venture China fund-raising starts.
newsitem.headline: BASF venture China fund-raising starts.

text.p: A group of Chinese banks have launched domestic fund-raising for a petrochemical joint venture between Germany's BASF AG and a state-owned Chinese partner, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Representatives of nine banks had met recently to begin raising money for the venture, which would be 50 percent owned by Sinopec Yangzi Petrochemical Corp, a unit of state giant China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), the agency said.
BASF would hold the remaining 50 percent stake in the venture, it said.
The integrated complex, to include a huge naptha cracker, has been valued at six billion marks and will be built in eastern Nanjing city on the Yangtze River.
The venture, known as BASF Yangzi Co Ltd, is intended to have annual capacity of 600,000 tonnes of ethylene.

Both investment partners had agreed to raise funds from the international money market, and in money markets in China as well as in Germany, where fund-raising began in October, Xinhua said but gave no details.
